surface: GET /api/v1/key (200 response, key with no cap)
authorization: Any key for the account; NOT management-only
origin: hand-written from the published OpenAPI schema; every value invented
notes: limit, limit_reset and limit_remaining are all null, which the documentation defines as UNLIMITED - not unknown, and not zero. An adapter must render that as 'no key cap' and must never coerce null to 0, which would read as an exhausted key. The point of this fixture: the key has spent 4310.77 with no cap of its own, so an unlimited key budget says nothing about whether the account balance can cover the next request. Reporting this key as 'unlimited funds' is exactly the conflation A04 exists to prevent. SCHEMA RE-VERIFICATION 2026-10-30: the authoritative OpenAPI schema for this route was read at https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/api-keys/get-current-api-key. Its `data` object publishes 24 required fields; this fixture carries all of them plus the optional nullable `expires_at`. Three corrections follow. (1) `rate_limit` is not an invented sub-shape: the schema publishes it as an object with three typed, required properties (`interval` string, `requests` integer, `note` string) and marks the object `deprecated: true` with the description "Legacy rate limit information about a key. Will always return -1." That description contradicts the schema's own example values (1h / 1000), which are what this fixture reproduces, so the field must be parsed and discarded and never read as a live rate limit. (2) `organization_id` and `workspace_id` are required and are the documented account and workspace identity: `organization_id` is "null when an individual account owns it" and `workspace_id` is "null when no active workspace resolved for it, for example because the key's workspace was deleted". (3) `is_management_key`, `is_provisioning_key`, `expires_at`, `creator_user_id` and `allowed_data_regions` ARE published schema properties, so their presence is documented rather than unverified; the abbreviated `Key` type in the limits guide simply omits them. `is_provisioning_key` and `rate_limit` are both `deprecated: true`. Two documentation conflicts are recorded rather than resolved: `is_free_tier` is described as "whether the user has paid for credits before" in the limits guide but "Whether this is a free tier API key" in the schema, so it must not be read as a plan name; and the schema documents only 401 and 500 responses for this route, with no 403, unlike GET /api/v1/credits. This fixture is the individual-account case: `organization_id` is null, which the schema documents as "an individual account owns it", while the account default workspace still resolves and `workspace_id` is non-null.
